description: Before Ezekiel says a word to anyone else, God tells him to let His words sink into his own heart first.
excerpt: We're fast to tell everyone else what they should be hearing from God. What we don't like is slowing down and letting God's words land on us first.
verse: "Then he added, 'Son of man, let all my words sink deep into your own heart first. Listen to them carefully for yourself.'"
body_html:
God tells Ezekiel to let His words sink into his own heart first. Before he says anything to anyone else. Before he goes out to correct a single person, he needs to carefully listen to those words for himself.

We don't love that order.

We're fast to tell everyone else what they should be hearing from God. Fast to correct, fast to point out what someone else isn't seeing. What we don't like is slowing down and letting God's words land on us before we hand them off to anybody.

I got an email recently complaining about an email my system sent out. Just a reminder to log into a dashboard. The woman read it wrong, took it as some kind of attack, and fired off something upset. My reaction was to go on the attack myself. Correct her. Explain how she'd misread it. Tell her she needed to grow in her spiritual life. Lecture her on being unoffendable.

I drafted my response. Had it ready to go.

Then I stopped and asked God to let His words sink into me first. It hit me pretty fast. I was about to correct her for the exact thing I was about to do. She got defensive about an email. My response was defensive about an email. The only difference was that mine was dressed up as spiritual correction.

That's what Ezekiel 3:10 is protecting us from.

If I'd sent that email, I would have felt right about it. The whole thing would have looked like me speaking truth, when really I was just reacting the same way she did. I would have completely missed that God wanted to deal with me before He dealt with her through me.

Most of us have done this. Had something to say to someone else before ever letting God say anything to us. And every time we skip that first step, we say things from a place God never sent us from.

Is there something you've been getting ready to say to someone else that God might want to say to you first?
question: Is there something you've been getting ready to say to someone else that God might want to say to you first?
